title: Support-extracted function vector as a shared packet plan
hypothesis: On held-out inputs for 16 synthetic state-transition functions, a support-extracted 16-dimensional function vector broadcast to all four packet slots will preserve joint packet accuracy within 0.03 and token NLL within 0.05 of an equal-width learned generic packet latent, while using at least 10% fewer actual serialized inference bytes and outperforming independent per-slot function codes in valid-path rate.
physical_object: One shared 2-layer MLP packet decoder and one support-pair encoder shared by all functions.
mirror_coordinate: Mean 16-dimensional hidden function vector extracted from the eight support input-output examples for the selected function; the same vector is supplied to all four packet slots.
logical_multiplicity: Sixteen support-adapted functions, each applied jointly to a four-input packet. Function identity is addressed by its support examples; no independent decoder weights are stored.

world.function_definition: Each of 16 functions is an independently sampled permutation over 32 states. A packet applies one selected function to four distinct input states.
world.packet_sampling: All 4-state query subsets and function IDs are generated from the world seed; no query input enters support encoding or training.

model.support_pair_encoder: Shared MLP: concatenate learned 16d input-state and output-state embeddings, project to 16d tanh vector; average the eight support pair vectors to obtain one FV per function.
model.packet_decoder: Shared MLP receives a learned 16d input-state embedding, the function code, and a learned 4-slot phase embedding; 2-layer hidden width 32, predicts one of 32 output states per slot.
model.generic_packet_latent_control: Same decoder and 16d width; per-function latent vectors optimized directly on support packets, with no support-pair encoder.
model.ptp_control: Same decoder with four independent per-slot function-code inputs; at inference, each slot receives the same function identity auxiliary, as in a PTP-style slot-addressed control. Charge the complete slot-code path and report repeated address bits per packet.
model.independent_upper: Serialized direct function lookup table over all 16x32 input-state pairs; actual int8 mapping bytes plus metadata.

controls: Support-extracted function vectors broadcast to all four slots (Mirror candidate)
Equal-width learned generic packet latent bank

training.selection: Choose one common update count and LR minimizing mean held-out packet joint NLL for the Mirror candidate across both dev worlds; same selection applied to all methods. If candidate is not viable under explicit gate at either setting, select by candidate NLL only and classify FAIL; fresh remains sealed.
training.shared_rng: Within each world and setting, methods receive identical generated support/query packets and minibatch stream.

secondary: actual serialized bytes including code extractor/code bank/decoder/metadata

gates.PASS: On both development worlds, FV is within 0.03 joint accuracy and 0.05 token NLL of generic latent, uses <=0.90x generic latent serialized payload, and is no worse than PTP in valid-path rate; deterministic replay exact.
gates.FAIL: Any quality, actual-byte, or native attribution gate fails.
gates.NOT_ESTABLISHED: Integrity, support/query isolation, deterministic replay, or payload accounting fails.

storage.authority: Actual uncompressed NPZ bytes of complete deterministic inference state.
paid_objects: support pair encoder weights for FV
all per-function extracted vectors or learned latent codes
serialized direct function table for upper

boundaries: Synthetic permutation functions only; no natural language result.
Function codes are support-derived and supplied to the packet decoder; routing/retrieval is not evaluated.
One four-slot shared-function packet does not establish arbitrary joint sequence modeling.
A function vector is not credited for code multiplicity; quality, bytes and valid-path controls determine the result.
Fresh worlds remain sealed unless all frozen gates pass on both development worlds.
